A short guide to pet carriers at the skyport
The desk wrote this for travelers
Pet carrier checks at Aurelia Skyways

Bring your pet carrier to the Companion Animal Travel Desk before boarding so the team can inspect it and confirm it is ready for travel. A good carrier should be sturdy, well ventilated, and easy to secure. It should give your animal enough room to stand, turn, and lie down without strain, and it should close in a way that stays fastened during handling.

If you are traveling with a cat, <<FACT F067>> Make sure the carrier is clean and dry, with no loose parts, sharp edges, or broken latches. Soft bedding can help keep the space calm, and a familiar blanket may reduce stress for some animals. Food and water are handled according to the route and the animal's needs, so follow the desk guidance before you arrive.

Label the carrier clearly with the traveler's contact details and keep the tag easy to read. Use plain, secure locks or fasteners that staff can open when needed. Do not overload the carrier with extra items, since open space inside matters for safe movement and airflow. If your pet is anxious, take a little extra care when placing the carrier on the counter and when lifting it into the vehicle.

The cabin team monitors animals during flight, and the carrier must stay closed for the full trip unless a crew member gives a direct instruction. Keep the carrier under the seat or in the approved place once you board. If your pet has special handling needs, tell the desk early so the team can plan the right support and avoid delays at the gate.

If you are unsure about fit, material, or setup, bring the carrier to the Companion Animal Travel Desk for a quick review before departure.
